packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no min(1)/max length constraint, allowing empty or unbounded-length arrays to reach the handler and DB.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:172 — Returned `message` string is a hardcoded English literal instead of an i18n key, inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which returns translation keys (e.g. errors use "booking_not_found", "you_do_not_have_permission") for the client to translate.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — isTeamAdminOrOwner uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` (AND) instead of OR, so a plain team admin who is not also the owner is denied even though intent is "admin or owner"

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max length cap, letting any attendee/organizer add unbounded arbitrary emails per call, enabling spam/harassment via trusted calendar-invite infrastructure

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in `addGuests.schema.ts` with no `.max(...)` (and no other cap in `addGuests.handler.ts`). The handler then persists all provided emails (`createMany`) and triggers calendar attendee updates plus `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, so an authorized caller (explicitly including any existing attendee via `isAttendee`) can submit an arbitrarily large list and cause unbounded outbound email/invite activity and DB writes. This is a security/abuse risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no min(1)/max length constraint, allowing empty or unbounded-length arrays to reach the handler and DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min(1)`/`.max(...)`, so an empty array or very large array can reach the `addGuestsHandler`. However, the handler itself prevents the empty/ineffective case from hitting the DB by computing `uniqueGuests` and throwing `BAD_REQUEST` when `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, so the finding’s claim that empties reach the DB is not supported by the diff. The lack of an upper bound is still a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern because a large `guests` array could proceed to `attendees.createMany` unbounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:172 — Returned `message` string is a hardcoded English literal instead of an i18n key, inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which returns translation keys (e.g. errors use "booking_not_found", "you_do_not_have_permission") for the client to translate.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the handler returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, which is a hardcoded English string (diff shows this exact literal). Elsewhere in the same handler errors use i18n keys like `"booking_not_found"` / `"you_do_not_have_permission"`. This is an inconsistency in API response semantics, though it’s not a verifiable functional bug from the diff because the web client’s `onSuccess` toast uses `t("guests_added")` and does not appear to rely on the returned message.
